title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Summary of the National Courts Symposium on Criminal Trial Work for Maintaining Rural Stability
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Summary of the National Court Symposium on Criminal Trials to Maintain Rural Stability

Fa [1999] No. 217

To: All High People's Courts of Provinces, Autonomous Regions, and Municipalities Directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; all Intermediate People's Courts nationwide; all large-unit military courts; all Intermediate Courts of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

The Summary of the National Court Symposium on Criminal Trials to Maintain Rural Stability is hereby issued for your earnest implementation.

October 27, 1999

Summary of the National Court Symposium on Criminal Trials to Maintain Rural Stability

In order to implement the "Decision of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Several Major Issues Concerning Agriculture and Rural Work" (hereinafter referred to as the "Decision") adopted at the Third Plenary Session of the Fifteenth Central Committee of the Party, and to implement the spirit of the National Conference of Presidents of High People's Courts (hereinafter referred to as the "Shanghai Conference") held by the Supreme People's Court in Shanghai in August 1999 regarding the promotion of reform of the People's Courts and the practical shift of the work focus of the People's Courts to the grass-roots level, and to further explore and develop the work approach of criminal trials serving rural stability and agricultural development, the Supreme People's Court convened the National Court Symposium on Criminal Trials to Maintain Rural Stability from September 8 to 10, 1999, in Jinan City, Shandong Province. Attending the symposium were vice presidents in charge of criminal trial work and chief judges of criminal trial divisions from the High People's Courts of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government. Representatives from the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region also participated. Vice President of the Supreme People's Court, Liu Jiachen, delivered an important speech at the symposium.

The attending participants exchanged and summarized the situations and experiences of various local courts in trying criminal cases in rural areas in recent years, analyzed the current public security situation in rural areas and the characteristics of criminal cases and peasant crimes in rural areas, and seriously discussed several issues that should be noted when trying several types of major criminal cases and peasant crime cases in rural areas. They also put forward clear requirements for strengthening criminal trial work and maintaining rural stability in the current and future period. The summary is as follows:

I.

The symposium believed that rural stability is a solid foundation for consolidating the political power of the worker-peasant alliance and maintaining the long-term stability and security of the country. Social stability and agricultural development in rural areas are the social conditions and material basis for fundamentally changing the situation in which peasants have long constituted the majority of criminals in China's urban and rural crimes. Since the reform and opening up, China's rural areas have enjoyed political stability, steady agricultural development, and generally stable public security conditions, which is the mainstream. However, in some places, there remain prominent problems affecting public security stability that cannot be ignored. The main characteristics are as follows:

First, rural social contradictions have become more complex, with some leading to group armed fights and petitions, and others escalating into serious public security crimes; second, illegal religious and cult organizations are re-emerging in some rural townships; third, the disorder in rural financial and market management has harmed the legitimate rights and interests of peasants, seriously affecting rural stability and agricultural development; fourth, the intensification of internal contradictions among peasants due to production and livelihood issues, neighborhood disputes, marriage and family conflicts, etc., leading to criminal offenses, is relatively prominent. If this situation is not effectively controlled over time, it will lead to changes in the structure of the basic forces the Party and government rely on in rural areas, which is detrimental to the consolidation and development of grass-roots political power; fifth, evil forces such as "village tyrants" and "township tyrants" and feudal clan forces in some places are running rampant, and some criminal gangs have obvious characteristics of organized crime under the nature of a criminal syndicate, becoming a major threat to rural public security and stability; sixth, social vices such as prostitution and whoring, trafficking and drug abuse, and gambling are spreading in some rural areas, inducing various crimes. The above problems are common across the vast rural areas, some are very prominent, and they not only affect rural stability, reform, and agricultural development but are also closely related to the stability of the entire society. Particularly noteworthy is that the proportion of criminal cases and peasant crime cases in rural areas among all criminal cases and criminals in China has increased year by year. For example, among homicide, robbery, theft, and assault cases, peasant criminals account for the majority, and their proportion has been on the rise in recent years.

The above situation shows that the problem of peasant crime in rural areas has become an important factor affecting China's public security and social stability and determines, to a large extent, the direction of China's public security situation. Solving this problem in fact finds an important breakthrough for solving the crime problem in China. Seriously analyzing and studying these issues and proposing specific countermeasures are of great significance for solving rural stability and the national public security problem.

The symposium believed that the trial of criminal cases involving rural areas and peasant crimes directly affects whether the Party's policies and guidelines for rural work can be implemented. Properly handling such cases is not only a matter of trial work but also a serious political issue. Therefore, strengthening the trial of criminal cases and peasant crime cases in rural areas and maintaining rural and overall social stability should always be an important and urgent political task facing the People's Courts.

II.

On the basis of seriously studying the "Decision" and the documents of the "Shanghai Conference," combined with trial practice in implementing the Criminal Law and the Criminal Procedure Law, the symposium studied and discussed several important issues in trying criminal cases and peasant crime cases in rural areas. It unanimously agreed that a firm policy of severe and swift punishment must continue to be adhered to for violent crimes that seriously endanger rural public security, such as intentional homicide, intentional injury, robbery, rape, and kidnapping, as well as for gang crimes with the nature of a criminal syndicate. According to the characteristics of local public security, regular "strike hard" campaigns should be combined with focused strikes and special operations to maintain a high-pressure posture of "strike hard," effectively curb the spread of serious criminal activities, and make every effort to maintain rural public security stability. At the same time, unanimous opinions were reached on correctly applying the law, handling common and frequent cases in rural areas, and comprehensively and correctly grasping the Party's criminal policies:

(1) Regarding Cases of Intentional Homicide and Intentional Injury

We must accurately grasp the standard for applying the death penalty in intentional homicide cases. Whether to impose the death penalty for intentional homicide should not only consider whether the victim's death was caused but also comprehensively consider all circumstances of the case. For intentional homicide triggered by civil conflicts such as marital and family disputes or neighborhood disputes, the application of the death penalty must be very cautious and should be distinguished from other intentional homicide cases that seriously endanger public security in society. If the victim was clearly at fault or bears direct responsibility for the escalation of the conflict, or if the defendant has statutory mitigating circumstances, the death penalty with immediate execution should generally not be imposed.

Care must be taken to strictly distinguish the boundary between the crime of intentional homicide and the crime of intentional injury. In cases of direct intentional homicide and indirect intentional homicide, the subjective malice of the perpetrator differs, and the punishment should also differ accordingly. Although both indirect intentional homicide and intentional injury resulting in death cause the consequence of death, the nature and content of the perpetrator's intent are entirely different. It is wrong to impose the death penalty simply because death occurs, without distinguishing the nature of the crime and the content of the intent, a practice that has seen an increasing proportion year after year. Among criminals sentenced to death, the proportion of peasant criminals has increased. The above situation shows that the problem of peasant crime in rural areas has become an important factor affecting China's public security and determines the direction of China's public security situation. Solving this problem is actually a key breakthrough. Seriously analyzing and studying these issues and proposing specific countermeasures are of great significance. The symposium believed that the trial of criminal cases involving rural areas and peasant crimes directly affects whether the Party's policies and guidelines for rural work can be implemented. Properly handling such cases is not only a matter of trial work but also a serious political issue. Therefore, strengthening the trial of criminal cases and peasant crime cases in rural areas and maintaining rural and overall social stability should always be an important and urgent political task facing the People's Courts.

II.

On the basis of seriously studying the "Decision" and the documents of the "Shanghai Conference," combined with trial practice in implementing the Criminal Law and the Criminal Procedure Law, the symposium studied and discussed several important issues in trying criminal cases and peasant crime cases in rural areas. It unanimously agreed that a firm policy of severe and swift punishment must continue to be adhered to for violent crimes that seriously endanger rural public security, such as intentional homicide, intentional injury, robbery, rape, and kidnapping, as well as for gang crimes with the nature of a criminal syndicate. According to the characteristics of local public security, regular "strike hard" campaigns should be combined with focused strikes and special operations to maintain a high-pressure posture of "strike hard," effectively curb the spread of serious criminal activities, and make every effort to maintain rural public security stability. At the same time, unanimous opinions were reached on correctly applying the law, handling common and frequent cases in rural areas, and comprehensively and correctly grasping the Party's criminal policies. In the work, this should be corrected. Only when intentional injury resulting in death is committed by means particularly cruel and under circumstances particularly heinous can the death penalty be imposed.

We must accurately grasp the standard for "serious disability" caused by intentional injury resulting in severe injury. With reference to the "Standard for the Appraisal of Disability Degree of Work-Related Injuries and Occupational Diseases" (hereinafter referred to as the "Work-Related Injury Standard") promulgated by the State Bureau of Technical Supervision in 1996, the "serious disability" referred to in paragraph 2 of Article 234 of the Criminal Law means any of the following circumstances: the victim has a major loss of body organs, obvious deformity of organs, moderate dysfunction of body organs, serious complications, etc. The degree of disability can be divided into general disability (levels ten to seven), serious disability (levels six to three), and particularly serious disability (levels two to one). Level six and above is considered "serious disability." Before relevant judicial interpretations are issued, the "Work-Related Injury Standard" can be uniformly referenced to determine the disability level. In practice, the death penalty is not imposed simply because "serious disability" has been reached; the specific circumstances of the injury causing "serious disability" must be considered comprehensively, along with the criminal circumstances and harmful consequences, to determine the punishment. For intentional injury causing serious injury and resulting in serious disability, only when the means of the crime are particularly cruel and the consequences are particularly serious can the death penalty (including the death penalty with a two-year suspension of execution) be considered.

(2) Regarding Theft Cases

The focus of punishment should be on crimes that seriously affect and undermine rural economic development, such as theft of agricultural means of production and products from contracted mountain forests, fruit orchards, and fish ponds; theft of peasants' means of livelihood, seriously affecting peasants' lives and social stability; group theft, theft rings, and integrated chains of theft, transportation, and sale; and theft of materials from railways, oil fields, and key projects.

The ringleaders of theft groups, habitual thieves, repeat offenders, and those whose theft activities cause particularly serious consequences shall be severely punished according to law. Theft of production tools or means of production such as cattle, horses, mules, and tractors shall be punished heavier according to law. For first-time theft offenders, juvenile offenders, those who commit theft due to genuine livelihood difficulties, or those who actively return stolen goods or compensate for losses, policy shall be reflected with appropriate lighter punishment. Among them, if conditions for sentencing to public surveillance, a fine only, or probation exist, public surveillance, fines, or probation shall be applied as much as possible, differentiating according to circumstances.

The "household" in "burglary" as referred to in Article 4 of the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Theft Cases" means a living space relatively isolated from the outside world for family members and their relatives, including enclosed courtyards, rented houses for family life, tents of herdsmen, and fishing boats used as family living spaces, etc. Places that combine living and business functions shall generally not be considered a "household" during business hours.

(3) Regarding Cases of Rural Evil Forces

The revised Criminal Law has broken down the original crime of "hooliganism" into several specific offenses, with corresponding penalties stipulated, which is more conducive to cracking down on such crimes and easier to operate in practice. For acts that constitute crimes under the original "hooliganism" provisions of the Criminal Law, they shall be separately convicted and sentenced according to the specific offenses of the revised Criminal Law, and handled under the principle of concurrent punishment for multiple crimes. For gang members who are relatively fixed, who dominate a locality by violence or threats, oppress the people, collect "protection fees," forcibly collect debts on behalf of others, forcibly contract in violation of regulations, and openly confront the government, they shall be dealt with as organized crime under the nature of a criminal syndicate; if there are also crimes such as intentional homicide or intentional injury, they shall be punished under the provisions for concurrent punishment for multiple crimes.

(4) Regarding Cases of Sabotaging Agricultural Production and Harming Farmers

For cases of harming farmers that are brought to court, they shall be handled promptly according to law. When sentencing criminals, attention shall be paid to recovering farmers' losses to the greatest extent possible. If the defendant actively compensates for losses, a lighter punishment may be considered. For criminal private prosecutions initiated by victims, different situations shall be handled: if there are many victims, the local Party committee shall be relied upon, and coordination with relevant political and legal departments shall be made, and the case shall be handled through public prosecution procedures as much as possible; if the victim directly files a lawsuit with the court and meets the filing requirements for a private prosecution case, the case shall be filed and tried according to law. Concerning the standard for the amount of losses caused by the crime of producing or selling counterfeit or substandard pesticides, veterinary drugs, fertilizers, or seeds, before the Supreme Court issues a judicial interpretation, each High Court may formulate reference standards for implementation based on local specific conditions.

(5) Regarding Cases of Group Armed Fights Among Villagers

When handling such cases, great attention must be paid to policy boundaries. After the case is tried and opinions on handling are proposed, the opinions of the local Party committee and relevant departments shall be sought. While strictly acting in accordance with the law, patient and meticulous explanatory work shall be done, combining the handling of the case with the eradication of the root causes of the armed fight, to prevent accidents and new conflicts.

The facts shall be ascertained, responsibilities clarified, and penalties correctly applied. The focus of punishment shall be on the organizers, planners, and backbone elements who committed crimes. Generally, the organizers and planners of the armed fight shall bear full responsibility for the crimes they organized and planned; those who directly carried out the criminal acts shall be responsible for the criminal acts they committed. Attention shall be paid to narrowing the scope of punishment and expanding the scope of education. For active participants who are accomplices, a lighter or mitigated punishment shall be imposed according to law. If they meet the conditions for probation, probation shall be applied; for those who were incited, deceived, or coerced into participating in the armed fight, whose circumstances are minor, and who show true repentance after education, they may not be treated as committing a crime.

Attention shall be paid to working with the victims. For victims injured in the armed fight, the illegal nature of their acts shall also be pointed out; for those who face difficulties in production or life due to the injury, assistance shall be provided to relevant departments to solve them, and efforts shall be made to properly handle the aftermath according to law, eliminate antagonism, and eradicate potential hidden dangers of retaliatory revenge.

(6) Regarding Cases of Abducting and Trafficking Women and Children

The ringleaders of criminal groups that abduct and traffic women and children and "human traffickers" who make a living by abducting and trafficking women and children shall be severely punished.

We must strictly grasp the boundary between crime and non-crime in such cases. For cases of selling close relatives, different treatment shall be applied: if the "adoption" of a child is for the purpose of profiteering through sale, it shall be dealt with as the crime of child trafficking; for those who, under the pressure of livelihood difficulties or influenced by the idea of favoring sons over daughters, sell their own children or adopted children, it may not be treated as a crime; if the circumstances of selling children are truly heinous, the crime of abandonment may apply; for those who genuinely act as marriage brokers and the introduced parties understand each other's basic situation, or who genuinely act as adoption brokers with the consent of the adopted child's parents, even if they introduced many people and received a considerable amount of property, it shall not be treated as a crime.

III.

On the basis of a careful analysis of the causes and characteristics of crimes in rural areas and peasant crimes, combined with the role and current situation of grass-roots organizations in rural areas, the symposium studied the policy boundaries to be grasped in handling criminal cases in rural areas and peasant crime cases, and reached unanimous opinions on correctly handling the following issues:

(1) Regarding the Correct Handling of Criminal Cases Arising from Conflicts in the Cadre-Mass Relationship

When such cases are tried in open court, the court shall generally go to the place where the incident occurred, carefully ascertain the facts, understand the true cause of the incident, clarify the responsibilities of both sides, and handle them reasonably, appropriately, and lawfully.

For those who use the power in their hands to oppress the people, act outrageously, and seriously harm the interests of the masses and the collective, constituting a crime, they shall be severely punished according to law; for those who merely commit a crime due to simple and crude working methods, after proper work and obtaining the understanding of the masses, they shall be handled with appropriate leniency.

For criminals who resist normal management by grass-roots organizations and purely retaliate against rural cadres, they must be severely punished according to law; for peasant defendants who commit crimes for a reason, a lenient policy shall be reflected. In mass incidents, punishment shall only be imposed on the very few ringleaders and organizers who constitute crimes; for other ordinary participants, education shall be the main focus, and they shall not be treated as committing a crime.

We must fully rely on the local Party committee and government, and fully solicit opinions from relevant departments on the judgment of such cases. For cases where the local government strongly requests the death penalty, the relevant background must be understood. For cases where the death penalty should be imposed according to law, the death penalty cannot be avoided out of fear that the defendant's side, being numerous, might cause trouble; conversely, for cases where the death penalty should not be imposed, it cannot be imposed simply because the victim's side is causing trouble. We must rely on Party and government departments to do a good job of legal publicity and education. Before the ideological work of the masses is completed, judgment should not be rushed.

(2) Regarding the Legally Imposing Probation, Public Surveillance, or Exemption from Criminal Punishment on Peasant Defendants

When applying penalties to peasant defendants, the principle of proportionality between crime and punishment must be strictly followed, while also fully considering the particularity of the peasant criminal subject. We must rely on the local Party committee to do the work of relevant departments, and appropriately apply more non-custodial penalties according to law. For those who have already constituted a crime but do not need to be sentenced to punishment, or where the law provides for public surveillance, they shall be exempted from criminal punishment or sentenced to public surveillance according to law. For those whose罪行 is relatively minor and who have a good attitude of admitting guilt and meet the conditions for probation, probation shall be applied according to law.

Efforts shall be made to cooperate with relevant departments to implement supervision measures for non-custodial penalties. In implementing supervision measures, various effective methods can be explored, such as strengthening contact with the original government and grass-roots organizations of the offender's place of origin in cities to implement assistance and education measures; in rural areas, education work shall be done through grass-roots organizations and the relatives, family members, and friends of the defendant.

(3) Regarding the Characterization of Crimes by Members of Village Committees and Village Party Branch Committees Who Embezzle Collective Property by Taking Advantage of Their Positions

To ensure the prompt trial of cases, before there are judicial interpretations, for such cases that have already been brought to court, they shall in principle be convicted and punished as the crime of embezzlement by taking advantage of one's position (职務侵占罪).

(4) Regarding Property Penalties

Wherever the law provides for a concurrent fine or confiscation of property, it shall be imposed concurrently. The defendant's ability to execute the penalty shall not serve as a basis for deciding whether to impose a property penalty. If it is truly impossible to execute or cannot be executed, the execution may be terminated or reduced according to law. For the principal penalties provided by law, such as death penalty, life imprisonment, and fixed-term imprisonment, with concurrent confiscation of property or fines: if the death penalty is decided, only confiscation of property can be imposed concurrently; if life imprisonment is imposed, confiscation of property or a fine may be imposed concurrently; if fixed-term imprisonment is imposed, only a fine may be imposed concurrently.

For crimes for which the law provides for a fine, the specific amount of the fine shall be determined based on the circumstances of the crime. If the Criminal Law and judicial interpretations have clear provisions, they shall be imposed accordingly; if there are no provisions, local courts may, in accordance with the principles of the law and specific circumstances, unify the reference standards for the amount of fines on the basis of summarizing trial experience.

(5) Issues Concerning Criminal附带 Civil Litigation

The scope of cases accepted by the People's Courts in trying ancillary civil actions shall be limited to material losses suffered by the victim due to infringement of personal rights by the criminal act and damage to property by the criminal act, and shall not include material losses suffered by the victim due to the criminal's illegal possession or disposal of the victim's property. Material losses suffered by the victim due to the criminal's illegal possession or disposal of the victim's property shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of Article 64 of the Criminal Law, that is, through the recovery of stolen money and goods and the order for restitution. If the stolen money and goods are still in existence, they shall be recovered in all cases; if they have been used up, destroyed, or squandered, an order for restitution shall be made. Where restitution of stolen property is impossible, this shall be considered as a discretionary circumstance for heavier punishment when determining the penalty.

Regarding the scope of compensation in ancillary civil actions, prior to the availability of judicial interpretation, the following principles shall be observed: First, full use shall be made of existing legal provisions to compensate the victim for material losses suffered as a result of the criminal act to the greatest extent possible within the limits permitted by law. Material losses shall include both losses already caused and losses that will inevitably be suffered in the future. Second, compensation is limited to material losses directly caused by the criminal act, and does not include mental losses or indirectly caused material losses. Third, the defendant's ability to pay compensation shall be given appropriate consideration. The defendant's ability to pay includes both current ability and future ability; for minor defendants, the ability to pay of their guardians shall also be considered, so as to avoid negative effects of large nominal judgments that cannot be enforced. The defendant's civil compensation situation may be considered as a discretionary circumstance for sentencing. Fourth, the lawful rights and interests of the victim shall be effectively protected. Where the plaintiff in the ancillary civil action brings a lawsuit, civil liability for compensation shall also be pursued against joint perpetrators whose acts do not constitute a crime. A minor perpetrator shall bear liability for compensation through his legal representative or guardian. However, co-defendants who are at large shall not be listed as defendants in the ancillary civil action. Regarding the apportionment of compensation liability: joint perpetrators shall bear joint and several liability for compensation; where a crime occurs within an entity such as a school and causes losses to the victim, the school or such entity that bears fault liability for management shall have liability for compensation, but shall not bear joint and several liability; in cases of traffic accident crimes, the owner (entity) of the vehicle shall bear liability for compensation by substitution or advancement when the criminal lacks capacity to pay compensation.

(6) Issues Concerning Private Prosecution Cases

The filing stage of private prosecution cases shall be strictly managed. Some localities, for the convenience of specific operation, have formulated specific filing standards; other localities have implemented "filing hearings," allowing the collegial panel to hear opinions from relevant parties and examine evidence materials to decide whether to accept the case. These practices may be further summarized, and if effective, may be gradually promoted.

Attention shall be paid to guiding and assisting both parties in collecting and presenting evidence on their own. Given that the general public of farmers still have a relatively low level of legal knowledge and face considerable difficulty in individual evidence collection, it is generally difficult to meet the evidentiary requirements prescribed by law. If a private prosecution case is simply and rashly rejected for lack of evidence, it may lead to intensified conflicts and trigger new criminal cases. Therefore, where the evidence presented by the parties is insufficient, on the basis of guiding the private prosecutor in evidence collection, if there are indeed difficulties, the People's Court shall investigate and collect evidence in accordance with law.

Mediation shall be correctly applied. Mediation shall be conducted on the basis of ascertaining the facts and clarifying liability, voluntarily by both parties, and in accordance with law. Forced mediation or illegal mediation shall not be allowed.

Compulsory measures and penalties shall be correctly applied. If, upon preliminary examination, a private prosecution case is preliminarily determined to constitute a crime and is relatively serious, compulsory measures shall be promptly taken in accordance with law against defendants who may evade criminal and civil liability. For defendants who may be sentenced to public surveillance or criminal detention, or to supplementary punishment only, or who can appear in court in a timely manner without posing a danger to society, arrest shall not be ordered. In imposing punishment, non-custodial penalties shall be applied as much as possible in accordance with law to defendants in private prosecution cases.
